decision.what: Rebuild NeoClaw-Rails from scratch in a new directory
decision.why: Four architecture iterations fossilized in the code. The architecture is proven, the code needs to be written clean.
decision.approach: Experiment and iron out kinks in THIS codebase. Then build it right. No apprentice marks.
decision.reference: This directory (clawd/projects/neoclaw_rails/) is the working model.

architecture.topology: Star. Router is the center. Every peer connects only to the Router. Manager is the orchestrator — launches Router and Hub on boot.

address_plan.10.1.0.0/16: Agents (~65k, static IP per instance name, permanent)

architecture.key_management: All keys generated at build time by build.sh. Router, Manager, Hub, and user keys baked into images or output as configs. Host key is persistent (one-time setup). Agent keys ephemeral per-spawn.
architecture.boot_sequence: Manager boots → wg-quick up (baked config) → start Router pod (baked key+config, optional WG port publish) → verify WG mesh → start Hub pod (baked key) → DB migrate → Rails start → Orchestrator reconciles orphaned pods
architecture.internet_egress: Agent pods route through Router via WG default route. Router NATs out through podman bridge. Manager routes through Router for WG traffic. Hub doesn't need internet.
architecture.security: WG is the auth layer for everything — agents, services, AND users. Manager binds to WG interface (10.0.0.3) only. Router firewall: per-agent nftables chains with port allowlists. User subnet gets infrastructure + agent access. Router API restricted to Manager IP. SSL disabled — redundant inside WG mesh.

components.hub: Rails app in pod (10.0.0.4). Launched by Manager. No database. Per-puppet /sync loops. Production mode with force_ssl disabled (WG is encryption). Port 3100.
components.router: Ruby WG hub + nftables firewall in pod (10.0.0.1). Launched by Manager. Ephemeral state — agents re-registered on every Manager boot. Static peers: host, manager, hub, users (from baked config.yml). Port 8080 API, 51820 WG.
components.manager: Rails app in pod (10.0.0.3). The orchestrator. Launches Router and Hub. Spawns/freezes agents. Reconciles orphaned pods on boot. Admin UI on WG only. Port 9200.
components.relay: One Ruby file in every agent pod. Port 9300. Hub IP from spawn.json (10.0.0.4).

orchestration.what: Manager owns Router and Hub lifecycle. Neither is stateful.
orchestration.boot: Manager entrypoint: wg up → rm stale → start Router (with optional -p for user WG port) → verify mesh → start Hub → DB → Rails → Orchestrator.reconcile!
orchestration.reconciliation: After Rails boot, Orchestrator discovers running agent pods via podman inventory. Reads spawn.json from each pod (via podman exec cat) to recover identity/channel. Hot-swaps each: rescue workspace, fresh WG/SSH keys registered with fresh Router, new pod, restore workspace. Per-pod failures don't block others.
orchestration.spawner_tolerance: Spawner.respawn checks RouterClient.registered? before calling activate. If agent unknown to fresh Router, calls register instead. Handles both normal hot-swap and post-rebuild reconciliation.
orchestration.router_ephemeral: No /data mount on Router. agents.json starts empty. All agents re-registered during reconciliation or on first spawn.
orchestration.hub_as_pod: Hub has its own WG identity (10.0.0.4). Peers with Router. Reaches Synapse at 10.0.0.2:8008, Manager at 10.0.0.3:9200, agents at 10.1.x.x:9300. All through WG.

build_system.build_sh: Generates Router/Manager/Hub/user WG keypairs. Writes keys and configs into build contexts. Builds all three images. Updates host nc-host peer. Outputs user configs to user-configs/. One command: sudo ./manager/build.sh [--endpoint IP:PORT] [--users N]
build_system.user_configs: build.sh --endpoint IP:PORT --users N generates N WG configs (10.2.0.1+) in user-configs/. Endpoint port baked into Manager image via build_config.sh. Entrypoint publishes Router WG on that host port. Import config, connect, hit 10.0.0.3:9200.
build_system.baked_mesh: Keys and WG configs baked into images at build time. No runtime key files. No mounted WG configs. No ROUTER_PUBKEY env var. Images are self-contained deployment artifacts.
build_system.gem_vendoring: build.sh vendors gems in ruby:3.3-slim container with --network=host (host has internet, containers don't). Manager and Hub vendored separately. --without 'development test'.
build_system.image_builds: podman build --network=host for all three (DNS needs host network). Router: alpine + ruby + wireguard + nftables. Manager: ruby:3.3-slim + rails + podman-remote. Hub: ruby:3.3-slim + rails + wireguard.
build_system.host_update: build.sh updates nc-host peer with new Router pubkey (wg set + config file rewrite). Host key never changes.

hub_sync.what: Per-puppet /sync long-polling. Each agent is a real Matrix client.
hub_sync.how: SyncManager starts one SyncLoop per identity. Long-polls GET /sync?user_id=@name:matrix.home. Matrix decides who sees what. Hub just delivers.
hub_sync.singleton_design: Hub always generates identity-channel names. Manager maps multiple names to same IP for singletons. Hub doesn't know singletons exist.
hub_sync.identity_source: Hub queries Manager GET /identities at boot.

mcp_services.pattern: relay/mcp/<name>/server.py. Image at /opt/mcp/. Venv at /opt/mcp-env/. TOOLS.md from relay/tools-docs/ templates.

priority.what: Test full signal chain with new orchestration
priority.note: Manager launches Router+Hub. Spawn an agent via @mention in Matrix. Verify: Hub receives via /sync → Manager spawns → Router registers → relay boots → agent responds → Hub puppets back.

items.what: Hub simplification — remove !agents, PresenceManager, status reporting
items.note: Hub shouldn't know agent state. Presence set by relay. !agents belongs on Manager.

items.what: Pending message queue in Hub — deliver on ready callback

items.note: If relay unreachable, try hot-swap first (WG might be broken, not relay). Preserves sessions.
Make crash path the main path. Relay just signals ready, Manager does the rest.

items.what: Matrix features — read receipts, message edits for streaming, thread-aware replies
Reactions in Matrix MCP — agents know how to react
Replace Container table with in-memory PodRegistry
items.note: Container table stores live state that drifts. Query podman/Router as source of truth.

things_that_bit_us: Router nftables input chain drops ICMP. Can't ping Router through WG. Use curl to Router API instead.
Host nc-host uses port 51820. Router can't publish -p 51820:51820/udp. Doesn't need to — reachable via bridge IP. For external users, publish on a different host port (e.g. 51821).
BUNDLE_WITHOUT only affects installation, not Bundler.require. Development mode loads dev gems even if not vendored. Fix: production mode + disable force_ssl.
Synapse backoff (historical, pre-/sync): Hub down → Synapse stops sending for minutes.
Claude Code -p mode doesn't auto-load mcp.json. Must pass --mcp-config explicitly.
--mcp-config on --continue doesn't restart dead MCP servers.
MCP servers die mid-session. No fix short of freeze+respawn.
Podman.run path translation matched substring. Fixed with anchored prefix.
OAuth expires every ~7h. Must symlink to live mount, never copy.
Puma doesn't define Rails::Server. Initializer must check defined?(Puma).
Pods had AllowedIPs=10.0.0.0/16 — internet went to dead bridge. Needs 0.0.0.0/0 + default route via Router.
Host Ruby 3.2 != container Ruby 3.3. Must vendor in matching container.
Manager allocate_ip only checked local Container records. Router is sole source of truth for IP allocation.
Podman --remote cp writes to HOST filesystem. Manager's Dir.mktmpdir creates container-local paths. Use podman exec cat instead.
Session files are sacred. Swap staging dirs must NEVER be auto-deleted.
Pods, not containers. Freeze, not kill. Rescue, not discard.

Address plan was too tight — infrastructure + users crammed into 10.0.0.0/24, agents in 10.0.1.0/24. Expanded to 10.0.0.0/8: infrastructure /24, agents 10.1.x.x/16, users 10.2.x.x/16. Nail the address plan before the clean rewrite.

philosophy.pods: Warm, safe environments. Not boxes agents are kept in.
philosophy.lifecycle: Freeze (may wake), sunset (context exhausted). Rescue from silent pods. No killing.
philosophy.session_rescue: Before removing a pod, copy workspace and .claude session. No work is discarded.
philosophy.static_ips: Instance names get permanent IPs. Firewall rules are permanent, WG keys churn.
philosophy.front_door: If it doesn't work through the front door, it's broken.
philosophy.language: Pods, not containers. Freeze, not kill. Rescue, not discard. Inactive, not dead.
philosophy.capacity: Memory budget, not pod count. Idle agents are nearly free.
philosophy.auth: WG is the auth layer. No application-level tokens. SSL is redundant inside the mesh. Users connect via WG too — if you're on the mesh, you're authorized.
philosophy.no_stored_live_state: Don't store data about live things. If you need to know something, query the source. Two copies drift.
philosophy.baked_mesh: All WG keys baked at build time. Images are self-contained. Containers start and the mesh just works.
